slides.title: Every AI counselor on the market drifts out of protocol
slides.subtitle: It starts giving advice, reassuring, quietly diagnosing — the three things a trained counselor is taught NOT to do. Nobody scores for it. Nobody publishes a drift rate. ZenAI refuses to send a reply that drifts.
slides.note:
The thesis slide. Same slide in all three presentations.

If asked what's new: Woebot, Wysa, Youper, Replika and Ash all control drift with prompt instructions and hope. None of them score each response against the protocol and regenerate when it fails, and none publish a crisis-detection recall number. We do both.

Ground it in HIS references: NBK470241 is StatPearls Cognitive Behavior Therapy, and his other clinical link is Cleveland Clinic on ACT. Both are manualised protocols. Say 'we built to the references in the assignment' — that lands.

slides.title: Architecture — ten agents, four tiers
slides.subtitle: Safety rail runs on every turn, before any therapy content exists · the yellow box is the contribution
slides.note:
Walk it in this order, 60 seconds:

1. TIER 0, every single turn — Privacy redacts, then Crisis & Safety scores risk. Risk detected and we escalate: 988, campus counseling, and the conversation STOPS. No therapy content is generated for that turn at all.
2. TIER 1, the core loop — Orchestrator → Mood Check-In (the trained model) → Memory → Conversation on the ACT/CBT protocol → the Fidelity Monitor.
3. TIER 2 — four specialists the orchestrator routes to, not always on.
4. TIER 3 — the Progress agent, trends across weeks.

THE YELLOW BOX IS THE CONTRIBUTION. Every reply is scored against the six ACT processes before the student sees it; drift into advice, diagnosis or false reassurance is rejected and regenerated. Note the arrow looping back from the monitor to the Conversation Agent — that loop is the whole idea.

Built today: Orchestrator, Mood Check-In, Crisis & Safety, Privacy. Everything else is scaffolded and scheduled.

Keep diagram 2 (the one-turn sequence) as a backup slide for 'but how does it actually work?'

slides.title: Core area: the distress model
bullets: **Data** — GoEmotions (54,263) + an EmpatheticDialogues supplement → **86,868 examples**, 6 distress classes, held-out 15% split
**Trained and measured** — TF-IDF + logistic regression, class-balanced
**macro-F1 0.521**  ·  vs GoEmotions-only **0.445**  ·  vs majority-class **0.106**
Macro-F1, not accuracy — the set is 47% neutral, so accuracy would flatter and say nothing
**The finding we didn't expect to need:** GoEmotions has **no loneliness label at all**. `isolation` scored **0.00** — unpredictable. The supplement took it to **0.47**

**The finding we did expect:** `overwhelm` stays weak at **0.28**. We map GoEmotions' *confusion* onto it, and a student with three exams is overwhelmed, not confused. It needs its own labels, not more data
**In flight for Oct 15** — distilroberta fine-tune over the same split, and the recall-optimised crisis classifier
slides.note:
*** THIS IS THE 10-POINT SLIDE. ***

Rubric: 'Core areas: for AI/ML related projects, it means the model and training. GUI/front end does not count at this stage.'

EVERY NUMBER HERE IS REAL, measured on 2026-10-09. Source: models/distress/metrics_baseline.json, metrics_baseline_nosupp.json, ablation_summary.json in the repo. Do not change them without re-running training/train_distress.py.

Lead with the isolation finding — a class that could not be predicted at all, because the dataset everybody uses has no label for loneliness. That is a real methodological result and it is the most interesting thing on this slide.

Be straight about the last bullet. Saying 'the transformer is training and here is the baseline it has to beat' is stronger than implying it is done. If it IS done by Oct 13, replace that bullet with its numbers and say by how much it beat 0.521.

slides.title: The ablation — does the supplement earn its place?
slides.subtitle: Held-out 15% split · macro-F1 · TF-IDF + logistic regression, class-balanced
slides.note:
The money chart. Spend 60 seconds here.

The argument in one line: we did not just throw more data at it — we identified a specific hole in the standard dataset, filled it from a second source, and measured what that bought. +0.076 macro-F1, and one class went from impossible to usable.

If asked why overwhelm got slightly WORSE: because the supplement shifted the class balance and overwhelm's source mapping was always weak. We are reporting it rather than hiding it, and the fix is hand-labelling, not more scraping.
